title: Daily life
goal: Describe your daily routine, say how often you do things, and talk about getting around.

notes.p: Routine verbs in the present tense describe habits: {{일어나요}} (I get up), {{씻어요}} (I wash up), {{출근해요}} (I go to work), {{퇴근해요}} (I get off work), {{요리해요}} (I cook), {{자요}} (I go to bed). To say "and then", take the first verb's stem (the dictionary form without {{-다}}) and add {{-고}}: {{씻다}} becomes {{씻고}}. Only the last verb carries the tense and the polite ending. Frequency words go before the verb: {{매일}} (every day), {{자주}} (often), {{가끔}} (sometimes), {{보통}} (usually). {{별로}} goes with {{안}} to mean "not really": {{별로 안 바빠요}}.
ex: I wash up and then eat breakfast.
I usually get up at seven.

notes.p: "Before doing" is the verb stem plus {{-기 전에}}: {{자기 전에}} (before going to bed). "After doing" is the stem plus {{-ㄴ 후에}} after a vowel ({{퇴근한 후에}}) or {{-은 후에}} after a consonant ({{먹은 후에}}). The main verb comes last and carries the tense.
ex: I have coffee after I eat.

notes.h: At or in: two different particles
notes.p: Both can translate as "at" or "in", but they do different jobs. {{에}} marks a time ({{일곱 시에}}), a destination ({{회사에 가요}}) and where something simply is ({{저기에 있어요}}). {{에서}} marks the place where an action happens ({{회사에서 일해요}}, {{집에서 요리해요}}). {{에서}} can also mean "from", paired with {{까지}} (to): {{집에서 회사까지}}.
ex: It's far from my home to the office.

notes.h: From, until, around, and getting there
notes.p: {{부터}} (from) and {{까지}} (until) attach to times: {{아홉 시부터 다섯 시까지}}. {{쯤}} (about, around) attaches to a time or amount with no space: {{세 시쯤}}, {{삼십 분쯤}}. You {{타다}} (ride) a bus, subway or taxi, and the vehicle takes {{을}}/{{를}}: {{버스를 타요}}. To say "by", use {{로}} after a vowel or ㄹ and {{으로}} after other consonants: {{지하철로 가요}}. On foot is {{걸어가요}} (walk there) or {{걸어서}} (by walking).
ex: I work from nine to five.
It takes about thirty minutes by subway.
I take the bus to work.

notes.p: A final consonant slides into a following vowel: {{일어나요}} sounds like {{이러나요}}, and {{씻어요}} like {{씨서요}}. Before another consonant, a final ㅅ or ㅈ is said as a stopped t, and the next consonant turns tense: {{씻고}} is said {{씯꼬}} and {{늦게}} is said {{늗께}}. Station names gain a sound: {{역}} after a word ending in ㄹ is said {{력}}, so {{지하철역}} is {{지하철력}} and {{서울역}} is {{서울력}}. In {{정류장}} (stop) the ㄹ is said as ㄴ: {{정뉴장}}.

items.en: I get up at seven every day.
items.why: A clock time takes {{에}}.

items.en: I work at a company.
items.why: The place where an action happens takes {{에서}}.

items.en: The restroom is over there.
items.why: Where something simply is takes {{에}}: {{저기에 있어요}}. {{에서}} is for actions.

items.en: I work from nine to five.
items.why: "From" a time is {{부터}}; it pairs with {{까지}} (until).

items.en: I go to work Monday through Friday.
items.why: "Until" is {{까지}}.

items.en: I usually go to bed around eleven.
items.why: {{쯤}} = about / around. {{열한 시까지 자요}} would mean you sleep until eleven.

items.en: I usually get up at six.
items.why: Hours use native numbers: {{여섯 시}}.

items.en: I shower before going to bed.
items.why: "Before doing" is {{-기 전에}}.

items.en: After eating, I drink coffee.
items.why: "After doing" is {{-은 후에}} after a consonant: {{먹은 후에}}.

items.en: I work out after I get off work.
items.why: After a vowel, "after doing" is {{-ㄴ 후에}}: {{퇴근한 후에}}.

items.en: In the morning I wash up and then eat.
items.why: "And then" is {{-고}}: {{씻고}}.

items.en: I go to work by subway.
items.why: {{지하철}} ends in ㄹ, so "by" is {{로}}, not {{으로}}.

items.en: I usually take the bus.
items.why: The vehicle you ride is the object of {{타요}}, and {{버스}} ends in a vowel: {{버스를}}.

items.en: I don't really like beer.
items.why: {{별로 안}} = not really.

items.en: I exercise every day.
items.why: {{매일}} = every day.

items.en: The office is close, so I walk there.
items.why: {{걸어가요}} = I walk there.

items.q: A coworker asks {{보통 몇 시에 퇴근해요?}} You usually leave work at six. You say:
items.why: Hours are native ({{여섯 시}}), and leaving work is {{퇴근해요}}.

items.q: Someone asks {{회사에 어떻게 가요?}} You take the subway every day. You say:
items.why: A habit is in the present: {{지하철을 타요}}.

items.q: You want to say that you sometimes cook at home. You say:
items.why: Cooking is an action, so the place takes {{에서}}; sometimes is {{가끔}}.

items.q: You're in a taxi and want the driver to let you out right here. You say:
items.why: {{내려 주세요}} = please let me off.

items.q: A new friend asks about your mornings. You want to say that you shower and then eat breakfast. You say:
items.why: {{-고}} puts the first action first; a routine stays in the present.

items.q: A friend asks {{커피 자주 마셔요?}} You don't really drink it. You say:
items.why: {{별로}} needs {{안}}, and a habit stays in the present.

items.q: You want to ask how long it takes by bus. You say:
items.why: "By bus" is {{버스로}}; "how long does it take" is {{얼마나 걸려요?}}

items.q: You want to say that you drink coffee before going to work. You say:
items.why: "Before doing" is {{-기 전에}}.

roleplay.title: A day in your life
roleplay.setup: Your Korean friend Minji is curious about your daily routine. Tell her about your day and ask about hers.
roleplay.persona: You are Minji, a Korean office worker in her thirties. You get up at 6:30, wash up and eat breakfast, take the subway to work (about forty minutes), work from nine to six, and sometimes cook at home after work. You go to bed around eleven. Speak simple polite Korean (해요체) using mostly words from levels 1–8: routine verbs, 매일, 자주, 가끔, 보통, 별로 안, -고, -기 전에, -(으)ㄴ 후에, 부터, 까지, 쯤. Ask one question at a time and react briefly with -네요.
roleplay.opening_en: What time do you usually get up?
goals: Say what time you get up and go to bed
Describe two things in order with -고
Say how you get to work and how long it takes
Say how often you exercise or cook

roleplay.title: Getting around Seoul
roleplay.setup: You're at a hotel front desk in Seoul and want to go to Myeongdong. Ask the staff member how to get there.
roleplay.persona: You are a friendly front-desk clerk at a hotel in Seoul. The learner wants to go to Myeongdong (명동). It takes about fifteen minutes by subway from the station next to the hotel, about twenty minutes by bus from the bus stop out front, or about ten minutes by taxi for roughly 8,000 won. Walking takes about forty minutes. Speak simple polite Korean (해요체, with -세요 forms toward the guest) using mostly words from levels 1–8, and repeat slowly if asked.
goals: Say where you want to go
Ask how long it takes by subway or bus
Ask about taking a taxi and the price
